t.E1204.agn: In 2025 EFSA saw no need for a numerical acceptable daily intake (ADI) and found no safety concern at the reported uses. Mild undesirable digestive symptoms such as abdominal fullness, gas, bloating and cramps have been reported at intakes of 10 g a day or more; EFSA stated that these symptoms may occur particularly in people consuming high amounts from food supplements.
t.E1204.body: Pullulan is partly broken down by salivary and pancreatic amylase; the remainder is fermented in the large intestine and converted into short-chain fatty acids.
t.E1204.eff.0.t: Mild digestive symptoms such as abdominal fullness, gas, bloating and cramps have been reported
t.E1204.eff.0.w: Especially people consuming high amounts from supplements
t.E1204.prod: Produced by fermentation with the fungus Aureobasidium pullulans.
t.E1204.regx.0: Re-evaluated; no numerical ADI needed. Mild digestive symptoms may occur at 10 g a day or more.
t.E1204.summary: A polysaccharide produced by fermenting starch with a fungus-like micro-organism. It is used in capsules and breath-freshening strips.
t.E1204.what: Forms films and coatings and adds thickness.
